items.informal_name: Remainder Reconstruction via Monomial Sum for Monic Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {p q : Polynomial R},
  q.Monic → ∀ {n : ℕ}, q.degree ≤ ↑n → ∑ i, (Polynomial.monomial ↑i) ((p %ₘ q).coeff ↑i) = p %ₘ q
items.informal_description: Given a monic polynomial $ q $ and a natural number $ n $ such that $ \deg(q) \leq n $, the sum of monomials $ X^i \cdot (p \mod q)_i $ for $ i < n $ reconstructs the remainder $ p \mod q $, where $ (p \mod q)_i $ denotes the coefficient of degree $ i $ in the remainder polynomial.

items.informal_name: Equivalence between monic polynomials of degree $n$ and the submodule of polynomials of degree less than $n$
items.type:
{R : Type u} →
  [inst : Semiring R] → [Nontrivial R] → (n : ℕ) → { p // p.Monic ∧ p.natDegree = n } ≃ ↥(Polynomial.degreeLT R n)
items.informal_description: For any nontrivial semiring $R$ and natural number $n$, there is a canonical equivalence between the type of monic polynomials of degree $n$ in $R[X]$ and the submodule of polynomials with degree strictly less than $n$. This equivalence is established by mapping a monic polynomial to its lower-degree part (erasing the leading term) and reconstructing a monic polynomial by adding $X^n$ to a lower-degree polynomial. The operations are mutually inverse, showing a bijection between these two sets.

items.informal_name: First Component of Degree-LT-(m+n) Polynomial Isomorphism is Modulo X^m
items.type:
∀ {m n : ℕ} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Ring R] (f : ↥(Polynomial.degreeLT R (m + n))),
  ↑((Polynomial.degreeLT.addLinearEquiv R m n) f).1 = ↑f %ₘ Polynomial.X ^ m
items.informal_description: For a ring $ R $ and natural numbers $ m, n $, the first component of the linear equivalence between the submodule $ R[X]_{< m+n} $ and the product $ R[X]_{<m} \times R[X]_{<n} $ maps a polynomial $ f $ to its remainder modulo $ X^m $, i.e., $ f \mod X^m $. This corresponds to extracting the coefficients of $ f $ for degrees less than $ m $.

items.informal_name: Identity: $\text{ofFn}_n \circ \text{toFn}_n = \text{id}$ for Polynomials of Degree Less Than $n$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq R] {n : ℕ} {p : Polynomial R},
  p.natDegree < n → (Polynomial.ofFn n) ((Polynomial.toFn n) p) = p
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$ and polynomial $p$ over a semiring $R$ with natural degree less than $n$, the composition of the linear map converting finite sequences to polynomials and the coefficient extraction map results in the original polynomial $p$. In other words, $\text{ofFn}_n(\text{toFn}_n(p)) = p$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Lower-Degree Polynomial in Monic Polynomial Decomposition
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] {p : Polynomial R} {n : ℕ},
  n ≠ 0 → p.IsMonicOfDegree n → ∃ q, p = Polynomial.X ^ n + q ∧ q.natDegree < n
items.informal_description: For any non-zero natural number $n$ and any monic polynomial $p$ of degree $n$ over a semiring $R$, there exists a polynomial $q$ such that $p = X^n + q$ and the natural degree of $q$ is strictly less than $n$.

items.informal_name: Remainder of polynomial division by a monic polynomial
items.type: {R : Type u} → [inst : Ring R] → Polynomial R → Polynomial R → Polynomial R
items.informal_description: Given polynomials $ p $ and $ q $ over a semiring $ R $, the function returns the remainder of dividing $ p $ by $ q $ if $ q $ is monic (i.e., its leading coefficient is 1). If $ q $ is not monic, it returns $ p $ itself. The computation relies on classical logic to decide whether $ q $ is monic.
